request.prompt_preview: CASE FILE Question: Site S-SFX-001 in Sfax dropped off the air in the early hours of this morning. Is this an outage we need to escalate? Now: 2026-09-03 09:00 (Thursday, Africa/Tunis). Data after thi

parsed.title: Planned Maintenance on Site S-SFX-001
parsed.root_cause_summary: Battery swap performed during scheduled maintenance window MW-0001 causing expected site downtime.
parsed.confidence_reason: Directly evidenced by matching maintenance window MW-0001 timing with the KPI drop and anomaly alert, and the change log and external events were NOT CHECKED.
parsed.impact_summary: Site S-SFX-001 experienced a complete drop in availability and traffic between 03:00 and 05:00, recovering fully at 05:00.

timeline.event: Maintenance window MW-0001 started for battery swap on S-SFX-001 with expected impact site down.
Anomaly alert ALR-0003 began as availability, active users, and traffic dropped on S-SFX-001.
Maintenance window MW-0001 completed and S-SFX-001 KPIs and alert ALR-0003 recovered to normal baseline levels.

findings.claim: Site S-SFX-001 availability and traffic dropped to zero between 2026-09-03 03:00 and 2026-09-03 05:00.
Scheduled maintenance window MW-0001 for a battery swap on S-SFX-001 overlapped the exact duration of the outage.
Sibling site S-SFX-002 showed no sustained deviation in availability or active users during the event window.
No alarms were recorded on S-SFX-001 or its parent nodes during the incident timeframe.

hypotheses.reason: The outage perfectly aligns in timing with the scheduled maintenance window MW-0001 for a battery swap, and normal operations resumed immediately following its completion.

recommended_actions: No escalation required as the site outage was due to completed planned maintenance.
